story.title: Ukraine Strikes Moscow with Drones Amid Russian Missile Attack in Kharkiv
story.summary: Ukraine launched over 600 drones targeting the Moscow region, marking a significant air assault on the Russian capital. Concurrently, a Russian missile strike in the Kharkiv region of Ukraine resulted in the deaths of at least 10 people. Reports indicate that several individuals were also injured in the drone attack on Moscow.

timeline_highlights.title: Trump Announces Deal for Hamas Disarmament and Israeli Withdrawal from Gaza
timeline_highlights.summary: President Trump has announced a deal for Hamas to completely disarm, which includes the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza. However, the implementation of this deal is contingent upon Israel fulfilling its commitments from a previous agreement.

timeline_highlights.title: Ukraine Conducts Major Drone Attack on Russia, Resulting in Multiple Casualties
timeline_highlights.summary: Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks against Russia, targeting Moscow and nearby areas, which resulted in at least six fatalities. The strikes also hit a warehouse linked to a major online retailer. Concurrently, drone and missile strikes across both Russia and Ukraine led to additional civilian casualties, with reports indicating a total of at least 19 deaths from the combined attacks over the weekend.

event_overview.title: About Gaza Peace Deal
event_overview.subject: Gaza Peace Deal
event_overview.summary: The Gaza Peace Deal refers to the U.S.-backed, internationally supported framework to end the Israel-Hamas war in Gaza through a ceasefire, hostage and detainee releases, Hamas’s disarmament and Gaza’s demilitarization, Israeli withdrawals tied to agreed milestones, humanitarian access, and postwar governance and reconstruction. It builds on earlier Egypt-, Qatar-, and U.S.-mediated ceasefire efforts, but its implementation depends on compliance and verification by multiple parties rather than on a single self-executing agreement.

facts.label: Framework and international status
facts.value: President Trump’s Comprehensive Plan is a 20-point roadmap; the United Nations Security Council endorsed the plan in Resolution 2803 (2025) and welcomed a Board of Peace to support its implementation.

facts.label: Core proposed exchange and military step
facts.value: The framework envisages an end to military operations and a staged Israeli withdrawal, alongside the return of hostages and the release of specified Palestinian detainees; further withdrawal is linked to agreed demilitarization standards, milestones, and timeframes.

facts.label: Disarmament and transitional governance
facts.value: A subsequent 15-point implementation roadmap, presented by Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, the United States, and the High Representative for Gaza, calls for Hamas to end military, policing, and administrative activity and for the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) to serve as the transitional civilian authority.

facts.label: Institutions and outside roles
facts.value: The plan’s implementation architecture includes the Board of Peace, an Office of the High Representative for Gaza, the NCAG, and an International Stabilization Force intended to support security, demilitarization, aid delivery, and reconstruction. Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, and the United States are identified as guarantors in the UN implementation report.

facts.label: Legal and humanitarian context
facts.value: The International Committee of the Red Cross considers Gaza occupied territory under its effective-control assessment and states that international humanitarian law continues to govern protections for civilians and duties relevant to the territory’s administration and supply.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows reported late-July to mid-August 2026 developments concerning the deal’s implementation, Israeli-Hamas military and political responses, and one related Lebanon escalation; it is not a complete chronology of the Gaza war, all negotiations, humanitarian conditions, or the wider regional conflict.

explore_lenses.label: What changed on the ground after the strikes?
explore_lenses.title: A wider aerial exchange, with unevenly verified damage
explore_lenses.summary: The reported drone operation was nationwide in scale, while the Kharkiv strike produced an immediate, locally documented civilian toll. Russian-reported damage and casualty figures inside Russia remain less independently verifiable than events in Ukraine.

claims.text: Russia’s Defense Ministry said it intercepted 791 Ukrainian drones across multiple regions, Crimea and the Black and Azov seas; Moscow’s mayor said more than 600 headed toward the Moscow region and 180 were downed there.
In Pechenihy, Kharkiv region, the regional military administration reported 10 civilians killed and 17 injured, with homes, a café, post office, store and vehicles damaged.

OHCHR has said it cannot independently verify Russian authorities’ civilian-casualty reports because it lacks access to the Russian Federation; it calls for investigations wherever civilians are harmed.

explore_lenses.label: How did drone attacks reach this scale?
explore_lenses.title: Both sides are escalating long-range drone warfare
explore_lenses.summary: The attack fits an intensifying reciprocal campaign of long-range aerial strikes rather than a major reported shift on the front line. Ukraine says deep strikes are intended to impose costs on Russia and pressure Moscow toward a settlement; the humanitarian consequences are mounting on both sides.

claims.text: AP reports that Ukraine has developed and deployed domestically produced long-range drones over the past year, while Kyiv officials say strikes inside Russia are intended to make Russians feel the war’s consequences and pressure President Vladimir Putin to negotiate.

AP describes the current conflict as an escalating duel of long-range aerial strikes, with neither side making significant battlefield progress along the roughly 1,250-kilometer front, according to analysts cited by the outlet.

The UN human-rights office reported that long-range missiles and drones were the leading cause of civilian casualties in Ukraine from December 2025 through May 2026, while also noting reported Ukrainian attacks on infrastructure in Russia that caused outages.

explore_lenses.summary: The immediate public signals point to continued military support and threatened retaliation, not a confirmed pause in strikes or a scheduled negotiation. claims.text: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine would respond to the Pechenihy strike; the statement did not specify a target, timing or operation.

After reports that British-made drones had been used in attacks inside Russia, the UK Defense Ministry said it would continue providing Ukraine equipment for defense; Russia’s embassy in the UK said London’s actions would have consequences, without specifying them.

At a July Security Council meeting, UN officials called for an immediate, full and unconditional ceasefire leading to a just and lasting peace, while stating that no military solution can produce lasting peace.

story_report.summary: Ukraine launched a large drone attack toward Moscow as Russia carried out a missile strike on Pechenihy in Ukraine’s Kharkiv region. Russia’s Defense Ministry said it intercepted 791 Ukrainian drones across several regions and seas, while Moscow’s mayor said more than 600 were headed toward the Moscow region and 180 were downed there. Several people were reported injured in the Moscow-area attack. In Pechenihy, local authorities said 10 civilians were killed and 17 injured.

sections.heading: Pechenihy civilians and property hit
sections.body: The Kharkiv regional military administration said the missile strike damaged homes, a café, a post office, a store and vehicles in Pechenihy. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine would respond to the attack, though his statement did not identify a target, timing or planned operation. The UN human-rights office has reported that long-range missiles and drones were the leading cause of civilian casualties in Ukraine between December 2025 and May 2026.

Kyiv officials have said attacks inside Russia are intended to make Russians feel the consequences of the war and pressure President Vladimir Putin to negotiate.

related_stories.title: Murder Trial for Tupac Shakur Opens 30 Years After His Death
related_stories.summary: The murder trial for Tupac Shakur has commenced nearly 30 years after the rapper was killed in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas. Prosecutors allege that a former street gang leader, known as 'Keffe D,' orchestrated the attack as an act of revenge for the beating of his nephew. The trial marks a significant development in a case that has long been considered one of the most prominent cold cases in the U.S.
